questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be ﬁlled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

Everything is bright and beautiful, ______?
questions.solution:
**Correct option - 2**

Here, concept of question tag is brought under consideration. Since, noun 'everything' does not denote a person. So, pronoun **it **should be used. Hence, **option 2 **is the appropriate answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be ﬁlled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

They are terribly busy with ______ work.
questions.solution:
**Correct option - 2**

Since, subject pronoun 'they' is given, thus options 1 & 4 are clearly eliminated. Now, blank is followed by noun 'work'. This shows that possessive pronoun **their **should be used. Because object pronoun 'them' and noun 'work' cannot come together. Hence, **option 2 **is the appropriate answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four given alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.**

Rest on one's laurels
questions.solution:
**Correct option - 1**

The meaning of given idiom is to be so satisfied with what one has already done or achieved that one makes no further effort. This means to retire from one's active life. Hence, **option 1 **is the appropriate answer.

For example :- With TV sports coverage becoming increasingly competitive, the BBC should beware of resting on its laurels.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four given alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.**

Fallout
questions.solution:
**Correct option - 4**

The meaning of given idiom is the adverse/serious results of a situation or action. This may result to situation of quarrel. Hence, **option 4 **is the appropriate answer.

For example :- He's prepared to take calculated risks regardless of financial fallout.

questions.question:
**Improve the bracketed part of the sentence.**

The main (causes of this failure is) inadequate ability growth and character development.
questions.solution:
**Correct option - 3**

If we use 'causes' then verb 'are' should come. If we use 'cause' then verb 'is' should come. Likewise, **option 3 **is the appropriate answer.

questions.question:
**Directions: Improve the bracketed part of the sentence.**

If they (did not know their ability) and they do not know which sports they want to do, they will not learn to play any sports and will not succeed.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'do not know their ability'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

The given bracketed part should be replaced with **'do not know their ability'**

 
• The two verb phrases i.e. 'do not know which' and 'did not know their ability' are joined with the conjunction 'and' hence we need to keep these phrases in the same degrees i.e. present tense. Hence, we need to use 'do not know their ability'
 
• Also, this sentence is the conditional sentence the main clause is in the future tense hence, we need to use 'the present tense' in the subordinate clause.

**So the correct sentence is-** *If they** do not know their ability** and they do not know which sports they want to do, they will not learn to play any sports and will not succeed.*

questions.question:
**Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.**

His vision

P: hardly related to

Q: and goals were

R: the reality around him
questions.solution:
**Correct option - 2**

Clearly, sequence PQ is grammatically incorrect because preposition is either followed by noun, pronoun or verb. Hence, options 3 & 4 are eliminated. And, a sentence does not end with transitive word(that needs object). Hence, option 1 is incorrect. So, **option 2 i.e. QPR **is the appropriate answer.

questions.question:
**Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.**

Pollution needs

P: otherwise our future generations

Q: to be tackled seriously

R: would suffer a lot
questions.solution:
**Correct option - 4**

Since, starter ends with verb, thus it will not continue with modal verb 'would'. Hence, option 3 is incorrect. In option 1, sequence RQ is incorrect. And, option 2 does not make a meaningful sentence. Hence, **option 4 i.e. QPR **is the appropriate answer.

questions.question: Let us look at the positive and negative effects of peer pressure.television and other ______ of life
questions.solution:
**Correct option - 1**

The given passage is based upon how thoughts, behavior, taste, music etc of other people have a major impact on a person. This influence is called as peer pressure which either have positive impact or negative. This depends on the thoughtful analysis by the people themselves. Since, option 2 is clearly out of context. Now, 'other' is an adjective which takes positive noun if singular word 'an' or 'one' is not given before it. Hence, option 3 is incorrect. 'Thoughts' is already mentioned which means word 'ideas' will make a repetition. Hence, option 4 is incorrect. So, **option 1 i.e. walks **is the suitable answer.

questions.question: a ______ impact on the living
questions.solution:
**Correct option - 2**

As, article 'a' is given, so it should be followed by an adjective because noun(impact) is already given. Thus, verb 'follow' is incorrect. 

Now, 'impact' is always strong. Hence, we cannot use 'slow' or 'mere'(used to emphasize how small or insignificant someone or something is). Thus, **option 2 i.e. deep **is the appropriate answer.

questions.question: peers often ______ us to change
questions.solution:
**Correct option - 3**

Clearly, option 4 is eliminated because 'changing ways' is a plural noun, hence plural verb(**without s/es) **should come. Since, the whole passage is based upon peer pressure. Hence, it is given that changing ways of life of our peers(a person of the same age, status, or ability as another specified person) **force **us to change our ways of living. Thus, **option 3 i.e. force **is an appropriate answer.

questions.question: both, positively and ______.
questions.solution:
**Correct option - 4**

It is clearly that adverb 'positively' will be followed by 'negatively' to give a synchronization. Hence, **option 4 i.e. negatively **is the correct answer.

Also, peer pressure have both positive and negative impact upon us.

Clearly, peer pressure arises when we follow our peers blindly. Thus, **option 1 i.e. blindly **is the appropriate answer.
